newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC names Bogni as private banking head.
newsitem.headline: SBC names Bogni as private banking head.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) said it has appointed Rodolfo Bogni as chief executive officer of its private banking division.
He will also be appointed to SBC's group executive committee. The decision is effective July 1, 1997.
Bogni will succeed Ernst Balsiger, who will remain a member of SBC's group executive committee, SBC said.

Bogni joined SBC in 1990 as chief executive of SBC in London. From January 1996 to the end of March 1997, he took leave to study mathematics applied to options theory at the Centre of Quantative Finance at Imperial College in London.
A spokesman for SBC, commenting on the bank's private banking strategy, reiterated what bank executives said at a press conference earlier this week.
"The direction is... onshore business outside of Switzerland," he said.
Private banking is one of SBC's four major business divisions. The other divisions comprise investment banking, asset management including Chicago-based Brinson, and domestic retail banking.
SBC does not publish the amount of assets managed by its private banking division, but it, along with the other two big Swiss banks, are estimated to be world leaders in the business.
Bogni will be based in Basle, SBC said.
